name: Family Reach
head: Family Reach: what they want, what they hate, how they feel about us
about: Family Reach helps people in cancer treatment pay for everyday needs like rent, food, utilities and gas, so they can focus on getting better. 2026 is their 30th year and they are rebranding. Day-to-day: Ansley (Sr. Director of Marketing & Communications). Katherine reviews and approves with her. Client since Aug 2026. Our lead: Nick.

rel.note: Ansley reviews fast and answers the same day. On 5 Oct she put the Side Effects videos first: “Excited to get more edits from the Boston footage, but those can come after.” (Slack, 5 Oct)

nps.note: Family Reach has never been surveyed.

ver.note: Last 90 days: 5 cuts, all approved at V1. Small sample (n=5). Agency average V1.96, and 50% of agency cuts go past V1. The long Boston patient stories took several rounds of notes before that.

read.chip: Side Effects tone not landed yet
read.note: They like the patient stories. On the Side Effects shorts the first VO was too bright and the music too upbeat. They want these to feel heavy and serious. Get that right on V1.

quotes.q: We really want these videos to leave you a little shaken by the gravity of them.

The current one used seems much brighter than the seriousness of the videos we're needing to convey. The music is also too upbeat/distracting, and we're missing some of the shots we intentionally captured (the straight on look, the pictures drawn showing hair and not, etc.).
Can we get versions that cut this down to each question as it's currently edited and then has the end card? We'd love to feature these on social media question by question.
quotes.cite: Family Reach (Ansley / Katherine) · Frame.io, 30th montage V2 · 22 Sep 2026

quotes.q: remove 1:49-2:29; use that b-roll at either the :47 or 3:11 photo segments, and make those photo segments full screen vs. framed in the blue/orange
quotes.cite: Family Reach · Frame.io, Patty & Theo V6 · 25 Sep 2026

loves: Real families with real details: a bill, a job, a day.
Short social cuts they can post one by one, each with the end card.
Lower thirds that show who the patient is.
The shots they planned on set: the straight-on look to camera, the hair / no-hair drawings.
The new brand and the line “Because cancer is hard enough.”
Side Effects shorts that feel heavy and leave you a little shaken.
hates: The old Family Reach logo anywhere, even on a door in the background.
A bright, friendly narrator or upbeat music on the Side Effects shorts.
Missing shots they planned and paid attention to on set.
Photos in a framed box. They want photos full screen.
Logo cards with a visible box around the logo.
how_to_cut: Hook on frame 1. No card, no logo at 0:00. An opening card comes after 0:03 or not at all.
New brand only. End on the Family Reach 30 Year logo and “Because cancer is hard enough.”
Patient stories: one family, one money problem, one thing Family Reach paid or fixed. Warm and hopeful.
Side Effects scripted shorts are the exception: serious and somber, as the client asked. Male, traditional narrator. Low, restrained music.
A death, a diagnosis name, an ex-spouse or a child's age goes on screen only if Ansley already approved it.
Side Effects V1 is 16:9 horizontal. The 9:16 version comes later. Patient social cuts are 9:16, 1:30 max.
Never cut crew voices into scripted scenes. Never change a word of the client's VO or on-screen text.

perf.note: Instagram @familyreach reels, last 90 days. 4,981 followers. Public data, views only. Tap a reel to watch it.

rows.t: Matt Damon throwback, Cooking Live Boston
What legacy will you leave? (Make-a-Will Month)
Rent or treatment, 30 years of help

perf.foot: Only 5 reels in 90 days. Most posts are photos and carousels with 5–60 likes. The one outlier: a behind-the-scenes carousel from a 30th anniversary shoot (5 Oct) got 385 likes, more than 6× any other post. People like seeing the real faces and the making-of.

brand.note: No brand color codes are written in the client file. Use the new-brand files the client sent: the end card Video closeout (15).mp4 and the 30th logo set. Tagline: “Because cancer is hard enough.” Never the old logo.

## Typo-QA Glossary
_Canonical on-screen spellings for the `typo-qa` tool. Added 2026-09-07 (was unmapped -- Boston patient-story cuts were transcribing unprimed)._
<!-- PRIME (machine-read by extract.sh — exact canonical terms, comma-separated, NO prose) -->
PRIME: Family Reach, FamilyReach, Ansley Howze, Katherine Hartley, Nila, Jennifer Christianson, Amiyah Miller, Lisa Roman, Briella, Kristen Benjamin, Paisley, DSRCT, Dana-Farber, Boston Children's, Tufts Floating

- **Nila** — patient (Nila & Jennifer story). NOT "Nilla" (a Whisper mishearing — she spells it N-I-L-A on camera).
- **DSRCT** — desmoplastic small round cell tumor (Amiyah's diagnosis). NOT the generic "head and neck cancer" used in early planning docs.
- **Because cancer is hard enough.** — brand tagline, new-brand end card. No old Family Reach logo anywhere (rebrand in flight).

## 🎯 Goals & Preferences
_Per-video briefs carry the shoot-specific asks (lead angle, banned content, required beats) -- see each item's Monday brief, which wins over anything general below. This section is for durable, cross-video rules._

- **New brand only** — no old Family Reach logo, no old backlog footage, on any cut (rebrand in flight as of Aug 2026).
- **Sensitive personal content (a death, a diagnosis name, a divorce/ex-spouse mention) needs an explicit approval gate before it airs** — briefs for the Boston patient stories name these per-family; treat any "APPROVAL NEEDED" / "do not use until confirmed" note in a brief as a hard block, not a suggestion, and check the delivered cut against it every version.
- **Patient lower-thirds**: name + role only until a fact (age, diagnosis name) is confirmed by Ansley/the family — several 2026-08-20 Boston briefs flagged unconfirmed ages/diagnoses as "do not put on screen yet."

## Editorial North Star / Stated Content Goals

- **12-month content strategy** to build a reusable library: hero films, short-form social, evergreen assets — all aligned to the NEW brand (rebrand in flight; old footage is off-brand/overused — do NOT lean on backlog assets).
- **30th anniversary + rebrand moment** — top-of-funnel awareness is the stated pain; content must reach NEW audiences, not just existing network.
- **Anchor concept:** one core hook question unifying content across all shoots. Client worried a cancer-specific hook limits broader donor reach → keep the anchor question BROAD (donor-wide), per the 8/4 strategy call.
- **Mosaic-video concept:** 30 stories for the 30th anniversary (Atdhe 8/4 directive — slide added to strategy deck).
- **4 shoot days planned:** Boston, Nebraska, Mount Joy, NYC. Nebraska may piggyback the Sept 9–10 MHA trip (open question to Nick since 7/28).

## Key contacts

- **Ansley Howze** — client lead (shoot outlines, CEO thought-leadership scripting).
- **Katherine Hartley** — client stakeholder (approvals alongside Ansley).
- CEO thought-leadership lane in flight (scripting draft owed to Atdhe by Ansley).
